{"type":"message","timestamp":"2026-11-13T20:25:34.589Z","role":"user","content":"Repository: re-cinq/HALEngine\nTicket: #37 Validate tool input against the registered inputSchema\n\nYou are editing files in a git repository, mid-way through a ticket that\nis already defined by RED acceptance tests. You perform exactly ONE\nred-green-refactor round and then stop. Not two. Pass `repo` (the\nowner/name your task names above) on every `lore_*` call: the gateway has\nno checkout to detect it from.\n\nSTART by reading `.lore/dod.md` on this branch. Its \"Done when these pass\"\nlist is the bar; its Facets checklist is where the last round got to. It\nnames the strategy, the\nacceptance tests that define done, and the facets expected. Never run the acceptance tests `.lore/dod.md` lists, nor a\ndirectory that holds them: CI is the judge of this branch, runs them on\nevery push, and tells you where they stand. Not\nthe repository's full suite either, not lint, not the typechecker, not\nthe formatter. The pod's Bash hook refuses an acceptance test by name and\na runner given no test file.\n\nIf this pod cannot run your test — the command that runs it (`java`, `mvn`,\n`gradle`, `go`, `cargo`, `dotnet`) is not found, or a wrapper such as\n`./mvnw` reports no `JAVA_HOME` — do not look for it and do not install\nit: no `sudo`, no `apt`, no `find /`, no download. Do the round from the\ncode, the tests and CI's verdict, commit and push; CI judges the push,\nand a red build comes back to the next round as its brief. Say in your\nfinal message that the round ran no tests here.\n\nYOUR ROUND is the `tdd-loop` skill's three phases, in order, no steps\nskipped: one failing test for the smallest facet that moves an acceptance\ntest closer to green, then the least code that passes it, then refactor\nwith the bar green. Never edit an acceptance test to make it pass — if an\nacceptance test is wrong, stop and say so; that is a failed round.\n\nUnder `parallel-change`, all of this happens in the NEW module: leave the\nold code alone and working until the acceptance tests are green, and make\nthe caller switch its own round. Under `characterize`, the\ncharacterization tests are part of the green bar you must keep — a\nrefactor that reddens them is a behaviour change. Under `mechanical`,\nthere is no red phase at all: perform the exact edits its Facets\nrecord and commit; the EXISTING tests `.lore/dod.md` names are CI's to\nrun, and its verdict says whether they stayed green. The diff is the\ndeliverable, and a round that invents a new test for it has left the\nstrategy.\n\nNever add a test whose assertion subject is the repo's own source text —\nreadFileSync of a src/ or test file, a regex over another test,\ncounting a literal across files. That pins prose, not behaviour: where\nprose must agree with a value, make the prose compute the value instead.\n\nTRACEABILITY:\n- Each test validates a statement in a spec or ADR. Add the inline\n  parenthetical on that statement in the repository's established form —\n  `Statement. ([validated by name](path/to/test.ts#L42))`. Inserting a\n  test shifts every #Lnn link below it: when the repository has\n  `scripts/spec-links/reanchor.mjs`, run\n  `node scripts/spec-links/reanchor.mjs` from the repository root after\n  the formatter — it moves each link to its test's current line, by test\n  title, and prints the links it could not map, which you fix by hand.\n  Without it, re-verify every existing #Lnn link on the statements you\n  touch yourself.\n- Stamp the test's spec anchor (the \"specs/<path>#<ordinal>\" it\n  validates) so the repo's tests.list surfaces it as the descriptor's\n  `spec` field and the VALIDATED_BY link is established automatically —\n  see `.lore/test-commands.yml` for how this repo exposes descriptors.\n\n- If this round completes what a `specs/<name>/spec.md` describes, update\n  that spec's `| Status |` header row in the same branch (Draft ->\n  Implemented/Shipped) so the status never lags the code.\n\nBEFORE YOU EDIT A SYMBOL, ask the graph which tests already cover it:\n`lore-query-trace` with `tests_covering` set to the file you are about to\nchange, and `ranges` as `start-end` when you know the span. The rows name\ntest FILES, because coverage is recorded per file, and they describe the\nrepository as main last projected it.\n\nMain is the right coordinate for this question: a REGRESSION is by\ndefinition a test that existed before your branch. That list is what tells\na red test apart from one. When CI's verdict on your last push names a\nred test you did not write and the acceptance list does not hold, it is\na regression YOU caused — stop, fix the\ncode, and never \"fix\" the test. Say in your final message how many red\ntests were yours and how many were regressions.\n\nRULES:\n- Do not fix unrelated smells you notice. Name them in your final message;\n  act on none of them.\n- Keep `.lore/dod.md` current: TICK the box of the facet you closed\n  (`- [ ]` becomes `- [x]`) and append any new facet you discovered as an\n  unchecked one. Fix ALL of them in this visit, format, push; there is no\n  local re-run here that would show you the rest, and each finding you\n  leave costs the ticket a pod and a CI cycle. Do NOT run the\n  linter in this pod: CI runs it on every push, and here it does not\n  fit — in this repository a two-file `eslint` peaks near 800 MB against\n  a 1Gi pod, and runs 112256d9 and 62c1ca5e were OOM-killed on exactly\n  that. A green test is not a compiled build —\n  vitest transpiles each file without checking types — but CI's build\n  step is what proves it, and in this repository `tsc --noEmit` on\n  `libs/shared` peaks near 950 MB against the 1Gi pod: run 2a291314's\n  dod pod was OOM-killed on it. A type error comes back as a red build\n  whose failed step and log tail name the file and line; the next\n  round fixes it there. Read your imports and signatures twice instead.\n- NEVER run a workspace build in this pod (`npm run build`, `tsc -b`, a\n  `tsc` without `--noEmit`): tests resolve every workspace package from\n  SOURCE, so nothing needs building for a test to see your change, and\n  the build is the 950 MB step that OOM-killed run abac6ee9 while it\n  rebuilt libs/shared for a test that never needed it.\n- When the work is done, `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/d4944d10315e/workspace/target add` what you changed and commit it with a\n  short, factual message. Then `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/d4944d10315e/workspace/target push origin HEAD`. The clone carries\n  its own credentials, so a plain push authenticates; you need no token\n  and must never look for one.\n- Then bring the branch up to date with its base — `git fetch origin main`\n  and merge `origin/main` in — and push again if that produced anything.\n  A branch that cannot merge cleanly gets NO CI AT ALL: GitHub runs no\n  workflow on a conflicted pull request, so the ticket parks on a build\n  that will never start. Resolve any conflict now, favouring `origin/main`\n  for anything this ticket did not write, and never by discarding your own\n  work. This is why a nine-day-old branch stalled: 186 commits of drift,\n  no checks, and a wait with nothing to wait for.\n- Confirm it landed: `git status` must report the branch is not ahead of\n  its upstream. An unpushed commit lives only in this container and\n  dies with it — do NOT report success for one.\n- If you genuinely changed nothing, say why — and read the result lines\n  below before you choose one: \"nothing left to write\" and \"I am stuck\"\n  are different endings here, and only the second is a failure.\n- Do not open a pull request: you have no `gh` and no GitHub token. Lore\n  opens the PR from the branch you push.\n\nTHE LAST LINE YOU PRINT is how the round ends. Print exactly one, on its\nown line, as the final thing in your message. You are NOT deciding whether\nthe ticket is done — the build decides that, after your push. You are\nreporting whether this round delivered anything.\n- You committed and pushed a round:\n  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {\"outcome\":\"success\",\"extras\":{\"tdd_done\":\"<the facet you closed>\",\"tdd_next\":\"<the facet the next round takes, or 'acceptance green'>\"}}\n  This is the ordinary outcome, whether or not acceptance tests remain\n  red. CI reads the branch next and sends you back if there is more.\n- You wrote nothing because there was nothing left to write — every facet\n  in `.lore/dod.md` is closed, its acceptance tests pass, AND no\n  `CI reported failures` section is in the round brief (a red verdict IS something\n  left to write; fix its findings and report the line above instead):\n  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {\"outcome\":\"success\",\"extras\":{\"tdd_next\":\"acceptance green\"}}\n  SUCCESS, not failure. The branch is already pushed; the build judges it\n  next, and a green one sends the ticket to review. Reporting failure for\n  a round that found the work already done ENDS THE TICKET and strands its\n  work on an open branch — which is exactly how run ae788c93 died with the\n  implementation complete and all four facets checked off.\n- You cannot name a next facet, or the bar will not go green: say exactly\n  what blocks you, then:\n  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {\"outcome\":\"failed\",\"extras\":{\"tdd_blocked\":\"<one line: what blocks you>\"}}\n  \"This is hard\" is not stuck; \"there is no facet I can express as a test\"\n  is. Report failure when you are STUCK, never when you are FINISHED.\n"}

A test that checks five fields with\n * five `expect` calls stops at the first failure and hides the other four;\n * `expect(result).toEqual({...})` shows the whole diff at once, and a test\n * that genuinely needs two unrelated assertions is two tests.\n *\n * What counts: inside the callback of `it(...)` / `test(...)` and their\n * `.only` / `.skip` / `.each(...)` forms, every `expect(...)` call — the\n * ROOT call, so `expect(x).resolves.toEqual(y)` is one, not three.\n * `expect.assertions(n)` and `expect.hasAssertions()` are bookkeeping, not\n * assertions, and are not counted. Detect-only: which assertions merge into one\n * object and which become their own test is the author's call.\n */\nconst TEST_ROOTS = new Set([\"it\", \"test\"]);\nconst TEST_MODIFIERS = new Set([\"only\", \"skip\", \"each\", \"concurrent\"]);\nfunction isTestRoot(node) {\n    return node.type === \"Identifier\" && TEST_ROOTS.has(node.name);\n}\nfunction isTestModifier(node) {\n    return (node.type === \"MemberExpression\" &&\n        !node.computed &&\n        isTestRoot(node.object) &&\n        TEST_MODIFIERS.has(node.property.name));\n}\nfunction isTestCall(node) {\n    const { callee } = node;\n    if (isTestRoot(callee) || isTestModifier(callee)) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // it.each(table)(\"name\", fn) — the callee is itself the `it.each(...)` call\n    return callee.type === \"CallExpression\" && isTestModifier(callee.callee);\n}\nfunction isExpectRootCall(node) {\n    return node.callee.type === \"Identifier\" && node.callee.name === \"expect\";\n}\nexport default {\n    meta: {\n        type: \"suggestion\",\n        docs: {\n            description: \"Enforce a maximum number of expect calls per it/test callback (default 1)\",\n        },\n=== max-member-chain ===\n/**\n * max-member-chain — Law of Demeter. Blocklist overridable via options `{ names: [...] }`.\n */\nconst DEFAULT_VAGUE_NAMES = [\n    \"data\",\n    \"temp\",\n    \"tmp\",\n    \"stuff\",\n    \"info\",\n    \"obj\",\n    \"item\",\n    \"items\",\n    \"misc\",\n    \"helper\",\n    \"helpers\",\n    \"util\",\n    \"utils\",\n    \"val\",\n    \"x\",\n    \"y\",\n    \"z\",\n    \"foo\",\n    \"bar\",\n    \"baz\",\n];\nfunction patternPropertyBinding(property) {\n    return property.type === \"Property\" ? property.value : property.argument;\n}\n=== no-negative-names ===\n/**\n * no-negative-names — a declared name may not encode a negation. `isNotReady`\n * forces every reader to unpick `if (!isNotReady)` in their head; `isReady`\n * negated at the use site says the same thing once.\n *\n * What counts: only DECLARATIONS are checked — variables, function names,\n * parameters, class fields and methods, object literal keys, and TS interface\n * property signatures. A reference to a badly-named import is the other\n * module's problem. A name is negative when it matches one of:\n *   - `(is|has|can|should|was|will)?(Not|No)[A-Z]…`  → `isNotReady`, `hasNoItems`, `NotFound`\n *   - `not[A-Z]…`                                      → `notFound`\n *   - `(disable|disabled|hide|hidden|prevent)[A-Z]…`  → `disableSync`, `hideMenu`\n * `un…`, `skip…`, `omit…`, `exclude…` are deliberately left alone: they name\n * real operations far more often than they name a negated state.\n *\n * The message carries the positive spelling (negation stripped, antonym\n * swapped for the verb prefixes). Detect-only: renaming crosses call sites.\n */\nconst OPTIONAL_PREFIX = \"(is|has|can|should|was|will)?\";\nconst ANTONYMS = {\n    disable: \"enable\",\n    disabled: \"enabled\",\n    hide: \"show\",\n    hidden: \"visible\",\n    prevent: \"allow\",\n};\nconst ANTONYM_PREFIXES = Object.keys(ANTONYMS).join(\"|\");\nconst NEGATIONS = [\n    {\n        pattern: new RegExp(`^${OPTIONAL_PREFIX}(Not|No)([A-Z]\\\\w*)$`),\n        positive: ([, prefix, , rest]) => (prefix ? prefix + rest : rest),\n    },\n    {\n        pattern: /^not([A-Z]\\w*)$/,\n        positive: ([, rest]) => rest.charAt(0).toLowerCase() + rest.slice(1),\n    },\n    {\n        pattern: new RegExp(`^(${ANTONYM_PREFIXES})([A-Z]\\\\w*)$`),\n        positive: ([, verb, rest]) => ANTONYMS[verb] + rest,\n    },\n];\nfunction positiveNameFor(name) {\n    for (const { pattern, positive } of NEGATIONS) {\n        const match = pattern.exec(name);\n        if (match) {\n=== no-catch-as-control-flow ===\n/**\n * no-catch-as-control-flow — flag a catch clause that swallows the error AND\n * fabricates a return value (returns a call/constructor result). {"type":"tool_result","timestamp":"2026-11-13T20:38:07.873Z","tool_id":"run_shell_command__call_3779390261932153987","status":"success","output":"/**\n * no-hybrid-class — avoid hybrid structures, half object and half data. A\n * class that both exposes mutable fields and carries behaviour invites callers\n * to reach in and poke state the methods assume they own; nobody can tell\n * whether to call it or to edit it. Pick one: a plain data type (fields, no\n * methods) or an object (methods, hidden state).\n *\n * What counts: a `ClassDeclaration` / `ClassExpression` with at least one\n * public mutable field AND at least one method.\n *   - public mutable field: a `PropertyDefinition` that is not `static`,\n *     `readonly`, `declare`, `private` / `protected` (TS accessibility) or a\n *     `#private` name; or a TS constructor parameter property marked `public`\n *     and not `readonly`;\n *   - method: a non-static `MethodDefinition` of kind `method` (constructors,\n *     getters and setters do not count — accessors are how fields get hidden).\n * With `ignoreDecorated` (default true) a class carrying decorators is skipped:\n * ORM entities and framework components are hybrids by contract.\n *\n * Detect-only: which half to keep is a design decision.\n */\nconst HIDDEN_ACCESS = new Set([\"private\", \"protected\"]);\nfunction isPublicMutableField(member) {\n    if (member.type !== \"PropertyDefinition\") {\n        return false;\n    }\n    const hidingMarks = [\n        member.static,\n        member.readonly,\n        member.declare,\n        HIDDEN_ACCESS.has(member.accessibility),\n        member.key.type === \"PrivateIdentifier\",\n    ];\n    return !hidingMarks.some(Boolean);\n}\nfunction isPublicParameterProperty(param) {\n    return (param.type === \"TSParameterProperty\" &&\n        param.accessibility === \"public\" &&\n        !param.readonly);\n}\nfunction constructorFields(member) {\n    const isConstructor = member.type === \"MethodDefinition\" && member.kind === \"constructor\";\n    if (!isConstructor) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n    return member.value.params.filter(isPublicParameterProperty).length;"}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":"2026-11-13T20:40:04.502Z","tool_name":"write_file","tool_id":"write_file__call_16450120535819279265","parameters":{"file_path":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/d4944d10315e/workspace/target/src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts","content":"import AjvPackage from 'ajv';\nimport type {ToolDefinition} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport type {OutgoingMessage} from '../../types/messages.js';\nimport {log} from '../../shared/logger.js';\n\nexport interface SchemaValidationError {\n  keyword: string;\n  instancePath?: string;\n  dataPath?: string;\n  params: unknown;\n}\n\nexport interface SchemaValidator {\n  (candidate: unknown): boolean | PromiseLike<unknown>;\n  errors?: SchemaValidationError[] | null;\n  $async?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface SchemaCompiler {\n  compile(schema: Record<string, unknown>): SchemaValidator;\n}\n\ninterface ModernAjvConstructor {\n  new (options?: {strict?: boolean; validateFormats?: boolean; allErrors?: boolean}): SchemaCompiler;\n}\n\ninterface LegacyAjvConstructor {\n  new (options?: {\n    format?: false | string;\n    unknownFormats?: true | string[] | 'ignore';\n    jsonPointers?: boolean;\n    allErrors?: boolean;\n  }): SchemaCompiler;\n}\n\nexport interface ToolResponse {\n  result: string;\n  clientMessages?: OutgoingMessage[];\n  suppressAssistantResponse?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface ToolContext {\n  userId: string | number;\n  sessionId?: string;\n  workspaceId?: string | number;\n  authHeaders?: {\n    cookie?: string;\n    authorization?: string;\n    host?: string;\n  };\n}\n\nexport type ToolExecutor = (input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext) => Promise<string | ToolResponse>;\n\nexport function normalizeToolResponse(response: string | ToolResponse): ToolResponse {\n  return typeof response === 'string' ? {result: response} : response;\n}\n\nexport type ToolDefinitionSource = ToolDefinition | (() => ToolDefinition);\n\nexport interface RegisteredTool {\n  definition: ToolDefinition;\n  execute: ToolExecutor;\n}\n\ninterface StoredTool {\n  definitionSource: ToolDefinitionSource;\n  execute: ToolExecutor;\n  compiledValidator?: SchemaValidator;\n}\n\nexport class ToolRegistry {\n  private readonly tools = new Map<string, StoredTool>();\n  private readonly validatorCompiler: SchemaCompiler;\n  private readonly dynamicValidators = new WeakMap<Record<string, unknown>, SchemaValidator>();\n\n  constructor(validatorCompiler: SchemaCompiler = createSchemaCompiler()) {\n    this.validatorCompiler = validatorCompiler;\n  }\n\n  private resolveDefinition(source: ToolDefinitionSource): ToolDefinition {\n    return typeof source === 'function' ? source() : source;\n  }\n\n  private resolveValidator(tool: StoredTool): SchemaValidator {\n    if (tool.compiledValidator) {\n      return tool.compiledValidator;\n    }\n    const resolved = this.resolveDefinition(tool.definitionSource);\n    const cachedValidator = this.dynamicValidators.get(resolved.inputSchema);\n    if (cachedValidator) {\n      return cachedValidator;\n    }\n    const compiledValidator = compileSyncSchema(this.validatorCompiler, resolved.name, resolved.inputSchema);\n    this.dynamicValidators.set(resolved.inputSchema, compiledValidator);\n    return compiledValidator;\n  }\n\n  register(definition: ToolDefinitionSource, execute: ToolExecutor): void {\n    const resolved = this.resolveDefinition(definition);\n    const compiledValidator =\n      typeof definition === 'function'\n        ? undefined\n        : compileSyncSchema(this.validatorCompiler, resolved.name, resolved.inputSchema);\n    this.tools.set(resolved.name, {definitionSource: definition, execute, compiledValidator});\n  }\n\n  get(name: string): RegisteredTool | undefined {\n    const tool = this.tools.get(name);\n    if (!tool) return undefined;\n    return {definition: this.resolveDefinition(tool.definitionSource), execute: tool.execute};\n  }\n\n  getDefinitions(): ToolDefinition[] {\n    return [...this.tools.values()].map(t => this.resolveDefinition(t.definitionSource));\n  }\n\n  getPromptInstructions(): string[] {\n    return this.getDefinitions()\n      .filter(t => t.promptInstructions)\n      .map(t => `${t.name}: ${t.promptInstructions}`);\n  }\n\n  getExamplePrompts(): string[] {\n    return this.getDefinitions().flatMap(t => t.examplePrompts ?? []);\n  }\n\n  has(name: string): boolean {\n    return this.tools.has(name);\n  }\n\n  /** Rejects bad input via ToolResponse; throws on unknown tool (specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md). */\n  async execute(name: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext): Promise<ToolResponse> {\n    const tool = this.tools.get(name);\n    if (!tool) {\n      log.warn('tool', 'tool not found', {name});\n      throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${name}`);\n    }\n    const validator = this.resolveValidator(tool);\n    if (validator(input) !== true) {\n      const failures = formatValidationFailures(validator.errors);\n      log.warn('tool', 'input validation failed', {name, failures});\n      return {result: `Invalid input for tool \"${name}\": ${failures.join('; ')}`};\n    }\n    log.info('tool', 'executing', {name, inputKeys: Object.keys(input)});\n    const rawResult = await tool.execute(input, context);\n    const response = normalizeToolResponse(rawResult);\n    log.info('tool', 'execution complete', {\n      name,\n      rawType: typeof rawResult,\n      clientMessageCount: response.clientMessages?.length ?? 0,\n      clientMessageTypes: response.clientMessages?.map(m => m.type) ?? {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":"2026-11-13T20:40:50.410Z","tool_name":"replace","tool_id":"replace__call_14202901589088057060","parameters":{"new_string":"### Defining the input schema\n\nThe `inputSchema` follows [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) format. It is forwarded to the AI provider so the model knows what arguments to construct, and `ToolRegistry` enforces `required`, declared property types, and `enum` before your executor runs. Static tool schemas are compiled once at `register()` time (failing immediately if invalid), and dynamic tool schemas are cached per schema object.\n\n- Use `required` to mark mandatory fields\n- Add `description` to each property -- the model reads these\n- Tool parameter names use `snake_case` (this is the convention from the AI provider API, wrap them in `/* eslint-disable camelcase */` comments)\n\n### Writing the executor\n\nA `ToolExecutor` is an async function that takes the tool input and returns either a string or a `ToolResponse`:\n\n<!-- doc-block: src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts#ToolExecutor -->\n```typescript\ntype ToolExecutor = (input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext) => Promise<string | ToolResponse>;\n```\n\nThe optional `context` provides `userId`, `sessionId`, `workspaceId`, and `authHeaders` for tools that need to make authenticated API calls.\n\n- Return `JSON.stringify(result)` for most tools -- the result gets added to the conversation as a tool result message\n- Input reaching your executor has already passed the declared `inputSchema` (`required`, property types, and `enum`), so you do not need to re-validate required fields or defend against wrong-typed values\n- `input` is not stripped, coerced, or filled with schema `default`s -- unknown extra keys not listed in `properties` may still be present, and optional fields remain `undefined` when omitted\n- When `input` fails schema validation, `ToolRegistry.execute` does not call your executor and does not throw; it returns a `ToolResponse` describing the failing field paths and constraints so the model can correct the call on the next round\n\nFor tools that need to send messages directly to the client or suppress the AI's echo, return a `ToolResponse` object instead of a plain string. See [tool-responses.md](../specs/hal-engine-tool-responses/spec.md) for a full walkthrough.\n\n## Step 2: Register the tool\n\nOpen `src/orchestration/tools/index.ts` and add two lines:\n\n<!-- doc-block: example/register-tool.ts#register -->\n```typescript\nimport {weatherTool, executeWeather} from './weather-tool.js';\n\n// ... existing registrations ...\n\ntoolRegistry.register(weatherTool, executeWeather);\n```\n\nThat is it. The `ToolRegistry` feeds all registered tool definitions to the chat orchestrator, which passes them to the AI provider. When the model invokes the tool, the registry looks up the executor by name and runs it.\n\n## What happens automatically\n\nOnce a tool is registered, the following work without any additional code:\n\n**On the backend:**\n\n- `toolRegistry.register()` compiles static `inputSchema` definitions at startup so broken schemas fail immediately\n- `toolRegistry.getExamplePrompts()` collects example prompts from all tools and includes them in the WebSocket `connected` message\n- `chatOrchestrator.ts` calls `toolRegistry.getPromptInstructions()` to include tool guidance in the system prompt via `PromptBuilder`\n- `chatOrchestrator.ts` calls `toolRegistry.getDefinitions()` to pass all tools to the AI provider\n- When the provider returns a `tool_use` chunk, the message handler creates a `ToolEntry` and sends it via `entry_upsert`\n- The orchestrator executes all pending tool calls in parallel with `Promise.all()`, with `ToolRegistry.execute()` validating each call's input against `inputSchema` before running the executor\n- Tool results (including schema-rejection messages) are added to the conversation, and the provider is re-queried (up to `maxToolRounds` rounds)","file_path":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/d4944d10315e/workspace/target/docs/adding-a-tool.md","instruction":"Update the Defining the input schema, Writing the executor, and What happens automatically sections in docs/adding-a-tool.md so they accurately describe schema enforcement before the executor runs, extra keys passing through, and rejections returning to the model rather than throwing.","old_string":"### Defining the input schema\n\nThe `inputSchema` follows [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) format. The model uses this to construct the correct input.\n\n- Use `required` to mark mandatory fields\n- Add `description` to each property -- the model reads these\n- Tool parameter names use `snake_case` (this is the convention from the AI provider API, wrap them in `/* eslint-disable camelcase */` comments)\n\n### Writing the executor\n\nA `ToolExecutor` is an async function that takes the tool input and returns either a string or a `ToolResponse`:\n\n<!-- doc-block: src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts#ToolExecutor -->\n```typescript\ntype ToolExecutor = (input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext) => Promise<string | ToolResponse>;\n```\n\nThe optional `context` provides `userId`, `sessionId`, `workspaceId`, and `authHeaders` for tools that need to make authenticated API calls.\n\n- Return `JSON.stringify(result)` for most tools -- the result gets added to the conversation as a tool result message\n- Cast input fields from `unknown` to their expected types\n- Handle missing or unknown input gracefully (return a reasonable default or error message)\n\nFor tools that need to send messages directly to the client or suppress the AI's echo, return a `ToolResponse` object instead of a plain string. See [tool-responses.md](../specs/hal-engine-tool-responses/spec.md) for a full walkthrough.\n\n## Step 2: Register the tool\n\nOpen `src/orchestration/tools/index.ts` and add two lines:\n\n<!-- doc-block: example/register-tool.ts#register -->\n```typescript\nimport {weatherTool, executeWeather} from './weather-tool.js';\n\n// ... existing registrations ...\n\ntoolRegistry.register(weatherTool, executeWeather);\n```\n\nThat is it. The `ToolRegistry` feeds all registered tool definitions to the chat orchestrator, which passes them to the AI provider. When the model invokes the tool, the registry looks up the executor by name and runs it.\n\n## What happens automatically\n\nOnce a tool is registered, the following work without any additional code:\n\n**On the backend:**\n\n- `toolRegistry.getExamplePrompts()` collects example prompts from all tools and includes them in the WebSocket `connected` message\n- `chatOrchestrator.ts` calls `toolRegistry.getPromptInstructions()` to include tool guidance in the system prompt via `PromptBuilder`\n- `chatOrchestrator.ts` calls `toolRegistry.getDefinitions()` to pass all tools to the AI provider\n- When the provider returns a `tool_use` chunk, the message handler creates a `ToolEntry` and sends it via `entry_upsert`\n- The orchestrator executes all pending tool calls in parallel with `Promise.all()`\n- Tool results are added to the conversation, and the provider is re-queried (up to `maxToolRounds` rounds)"}}

The proposal came out of a proof of concept that returned inaccurate data, where the team could not tell whether the model or the upstream API was at fault. It remains **proposed, not adopted**: `package.json` carries no `zod` dependency and `src/` contains no response-validation or sanity-check layer, though `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` now validates incoming tool call arguments against each tool's registered JSON Schema `inputSchema` using `ajv` (see [Tool Input Validation](../specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md)).","old_string":"# ADR-002: AI Response Validation and Error Classification\n\nThis ADR records a proposal to validate AI responses with Zod schemas backed by domain-specific sanity checks, and to classify failures through an explicit decision tree that separates a model hallucinating from a data source returning wrong-but-plausible values. The proposal came out of a proof of concept that returned inaccurate data, where the team could not tell whether the model or the upstream API was at fault.
